messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Mounjaro may cost $25 for up to a 3-month prescription if you have commercial insurance and are eligible for the Savings Card. Note that patients with government insurance (Medicare, Medicaid) are not eligible for the savings card. Without insurance, Mounjaro can cost $499 for a 1-month prescription of single-dose pens (all strengths) through the LillyDirect Mounjaro Self Pay Journey Program. The list price of Mounjaro is $1,112.16 per fill, but this is not what most people pay.
Refer to our Mounjaro price guide for more information, or see " Can you afford Mounjaro without insurance? " and " What is the Mounjaro Coupon or Savings Card? "
Triplet: ["Mounjaro", "has savings card eligibility", "commercial insurance"]

The relation 'has savings card eligibility' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug's savings card is available to patients with the specified type of insurance.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has coupon eligibility': The subject drug may qualify for the coupon or savings program specified by the object entity.
B. 'used in population': The subject drug is used in or approved for the patient population or age group specified by the object entity.
C. 'has dosage form': The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
D. 'may be used for': The subject drug can be used for the purpose or indication specified by the object entity.
E. 'has availability': The subject drug is available under the regulatory status specified by the object entity (for example prescription only or over the counter).
F. None of the above.

Answer:
